findings.source_passage: When I saw the skunk, with his big sleek fat face, and thought of poor little Jane in his clutches, I felt real mad that I hadn't got a gun with me. I'd have tickled him up some.
findings.why_it_matters: The vivid physical description 'big sleek fat face' and the distinctly American idiom 'I'd have tickled him up some' are signature voice markers for Julius; the draft drops both, reducing a characterful moment to a bare summary.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'with his big sleek fat face' and 'I'd have tickled him up some' to preserve Julius's vernacular register.

findings.source_passage: I thought for sure you'd know all this... I began to think that there was nothing doing, that he'd just come on the trip for his health, but I remembered that he hadn't changed for dinner, though it was by way of being a slap-up hotel
findings.why_it_matters: The deductive aside ('he hadn't changed for dinner … slap-up hotel') is a small but rhythmically distinctive piece of Julius's story-logic that shows his alertness; the draft replaces it with a flat paraphrase losing the reasoning voice entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-insert the 'hadn't changed for dinner / slap-up hotel' deduction verbatim or near-verbatim.

findings.source_passage: He did the usual stunt. Said: 'What's happened?' And 'Where am I?' But I knew the answer to the last well enough. There's no moss growing on my brain.
findings.source_locator: Julius's story, waking-up scene after the fall
findings.why_it_matters: 'There's no moss growing on my brain' is a distinctively Americanised self-deprecating witticism that characterises Julius's voice; the draft omits the whole 'usual stunt' passage and the quip entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the 'usual stunt' beat and 'There's no moss growing on my brain' line, even in compressed form.

findings.source_passage: I fell, with a considerable portion of one of my trees, into one of my newly planted flower-beds.
findings.source_locator: Dr. Hall's reply about the fall
findings.why_it_matters: This is the doctor's most quotable and tonally distinctive line—dry English understatement—and Julius's follow-up ('I liked the man. He seemed to have a sense of humour') depends on it. Both are absent from the draft.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore Dr. Hall's verbatim formulation and Julius's appreciative aside ('I liked the man. He seemed to have a sense of humour. I felt sure that he, at least, was plumb straight') to preserve the comic register.

findings.source_passage: I made up my mind in a flash... I trotted out the stern guardian business, and a nervous breakdown, and finally explained that I had fancied I recognized her among the patients... I guess it was just the kind of story he was expecting. 'Quite a romance,' he said genially
findings.source_locator: Julius's story, explanation to Dr. Hall
findings.why_it_matters: The draft compresses the cover-story sequence into bald summary, losing the vernacular texture ('I trotted out,' 'just the kind of story he was expecting') that is part of Julius's colourful idiom.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'I trotted out the stern guardian business' and 'I guess it was just the kind of story he was expecting' to maintain Julius's self-aware narrative voice.

findings.source_passage: valiantly repressing memories of the steely glitter in Mrs. Vandemeyer's eyes
findings.source_locator: after Tuppence says 'Do you think I'm afraid?'
findings.why_it_matters: In the source this parenthetical is narratorial irony undercutting Tuppence's bravado; the draft folds it awkwardly into her summary of events rather than keeping it as a dry aside, losing the comic-ironic register.
findings.suggested_fix: Return it to its position as a parenthetical aside after Tuppence's indignant denial, not as part of her reported speech.

summary: The draft faithfully conveys plot but repeatedly flattens Julius's idiomatic American vernacular and Dr. Hall's dry wit—losing at least four medium-weight voice passages ('big sleek fat face / tickled him up some', 'no moss growing on my brain', Hall's flower-bed quip with Julius's appreciation, and the 'trotted out' cover-story texture)—which together constitute a pattern of voice erasure sufficient to require regeneration.
